summary.text: Transcription copies a segment of DNA into RNA so that a gene can be expressed.
An RNA polymerase reads the DNA sequence and builds a complementary RNA strand called the primary transcript.
Some of the RNA made codes for proteins, called messenger RNA, while other RNA is non-coding RNA.

facts.label: Four stages
facts.value: Initiation, promoter escape, elongation and termination

facts.label: Template strand
facts.value: Only one of the two DNA strands is read

facts.label: Base swap
facts.value: RNA gets uracil wherever DNA would have thymine

facts.label: Accuracy
facts.value: Lower copying fidelity than DNA replication

facts.label: Enhancer boost
facts.value: Some genes see up to 100-fold more transcription

items.prompt: A stretch of the coding strand carries a thymine. What sits in that spot of the RNA copy?

options.label: Thymine, copied across unchanged
Uracil, standing in for thymine
Adenine, its pairing partner
Guanine, as the strand reverses

items.explain: The RNA matches the sense (coding) strand except that uracil replaces thymine.

items.prompt: Compared with copying DNA, how accurate is making RNA from DNA?

options.label: Equally accurate, because both use the same proofreading
More accurate, because RNA is shorter and simpler
More accurate, because both strands check each other
Less accurate, because proofreading controls are fewer and weaker

items.explain: Transcription has fewer and less effective controls, so it has lower copying fidelity than DNA replication.

items.prompt: RNA polymerase reaches a stretch of double-stranded DNA. What does it use as the template?

options.label: Only one of the two strands
Both strands, read in turn and joined
A short RNA primer set on each strand
Nothing; it builds RNA from free nucleotides alone

items.explain: Only one of the two DNA strands serves as a template, and no RNA primer is needed.

items.prompt: A gene sits far from its enhancer on the DNA. How can the enhancer still boost the gene?

options.label: The enhancer is cut out and pasted beside the promoter
The enhancer's sequence is switched to match the promoter
The DNA loops so the enhancer comes close to the promoter
The gene slides along the DNA until it meets the enhancer

items.explain: Enhancers loop over long distances to come into physical proximity with the promoters of their target genes.

items.prompt: A negative-sense RNA virus needs positive-sense messenger RNA. How does it get it?

options.label: The host cell copies it from a DNA template
The host's DNA polymerase rewrites the genome
The ribosome reads the genome and splits it
Its genome acts as the template, copied by a viral RNA polymerase

items.explain: The negative-sense RNA genome is a template for positive-sense viral messenger RNA, catalyzed by a viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase.

items.prompt: Two tissue types run different gene programs. What helps explain this?

options.label: Each tissue deletes the enhancer regions it does not use
Each tissue brings only certain enhancers close to the promoters they regulate
Each tissue reads a different strand of every gene
Each tissue holds a different set of general transcription factors

items.explain: Enhancers control cell-type-specific programs, and in a given tissue only specific enhancers are brought next to their promoters.
